memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: “Be still, and know that I am God.” – Psalm 46:10

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
Many servants of God are running fast, but not waiting long. Busy in ministry but empty in intimacy. We preach, plan, travel, counsel, and organize yet slowly, prayer becomes short,
meditation disappears, Bible reading becomes preparation, not devotion.
We are soaked in ministry, but dry in the power of the Spirit. Leonard Ravenhill warned us that revival does not come through speed, skill, or schedules but through men who linger in God’s presence.
Planning without prayer leads to self-dependence.
Knowledge without kneeling leads to spiritual pride.
Activity without waiting leads to ruin. Jesus Himself though full of power often withdrew to lonely places and prayed. If the Son of God had to stop and wait, who are we to keep running? We may still be successful before people, but weak before God.
If we do not stop to wait on the Lord, soon we will not be over-running, we will be ran over.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: “The secret of revival lies in the secret place.” ...Leonard Ravenhill, Why Revival Tarries

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
“Lord, stop our rushing. Restore our waiting.
Bring us back to the secret place. Teach us again to sit at Your feet before we stand before people.
In Jesus’ name, Amen.”

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Ministry must flow from the Presence, not replace the Presence.

recommended_book.label: Recommended Book
recommended_book.title: Why Revival Tarries
recommended_book.author: Leonard Ravenhill
recommended_book.quote: A prophetic warning that activity without agony, and ministry without prayer, delays true revival.
